title: When a fake stands in for the OS layer, test the mode-to-OS-parameter mapping on its own
rule: If an activator or service is unit-tested through a fake of the OS layer (a Registrar, a FontActivator mock), the code that turns the app's own enum into the OS value (Mode -> CoreText scope, Mode -> registry key, flag -> API constant) sits below the fake and no fake-based test sees it. Give that mapping its own test against the literal OS values, and make the integration test prove the OS state of each mode (for example: unregister from the other scope and expect 'not registered'), not only that a second process sees the font, which every mode passes.
rationale: E6.4 (#77): swapping kCTFontManagerScopeUser and kCTFontManagerScopeSession left every test green — the fake recorded Mode, never called scope(), and the integration tests registered and unregistered through the same scope(mode).
